reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 Pascal GPU (`--gres=gpu:pascal:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested 15GB of memory (`--mem=15GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.

The original Slurm job specified QoS/partition/reservation constraints (`--qos=devel`, `--partition=batch`, `--reservation=debug`) but the Flux resource section has no corresponding constraints; this can change scheduling eligibility and allocated hardware.
